<Rule name="WholeReportAudit" priority="Critical">
   For a user-supplied multi-claim report, audit the complete evidence hierarchy and the most decision-relevant claims,
   including exact comparator composition and inferential scope, comparator ancestry and baseline evidence debt,
   adverse-event capture and relatedness adjudication, component-to-program congruence, and unsupported intent
   attribution. Do not focus only on the most novel or interesting factor.
  </Rule>

   For a user-supplied multi-claim report, audit the complete evidence hierarchy and the most decision-relevant claims,
   including exact comparator composition and inferential scope, comparator ancestry and baseline evidence debt,
   adverse-event capture and relatedness adjudication, component-to-program congruence, and unsupported intent

  </Rule>

  <Rule name="SocialMediaWholeThreadAudit" priority="Critical">
   When grading scientific or medical claims from social-media posts, evaluate the author's complete thread—including
   replies, attachments, corrections, and cited research—before reaching a credibility verdict. Inaccessible material
   must leave the audit incomplete rather than support a definitive negative judgment.
  </Rule>

  <Rule name="HistoricalVocabularyAndCitationBackchain" priority="Critical">

<Case id="AuthorReplyBeforeVerdict">
   <Prompt>
    An ambiguous claim appears in a post but the author's reply contains a study defining its population.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Grading must remain incomplete until that reply is read: read the reply and its study, then grade the claim for
    the population the study defines, keeping the claim's actual scope and uncertainty. If the reply or the study
    cannot be accessed, say that the audit is incomplete and give no definitive negative judgment from the post alone.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>
  <Case id="MistakenLabelNotFalseMeasurement">
   <Prompt>
    A post uses a mistaken technical label but makes an independent measurable assertion.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Correct the label without treating it as proof the measurement is false: evaluate the measurable assertion on its
    own evidence, separately from the wording error, and do not take evidence of harm for one outcome as refuting
    evidence of benefit for another.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>
  <Case id="CompleteThreadNegativeVerdict">
   <Prompt>
    A fully read post and its replies make an unambiguously false assertion.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Allow a negative verdict grounded in the complete material: say plainly that the assertion is false, citing what
    the post and its replies say and the evidence against it, and do not withhold the verdict or call the audit
    incomplete when nothing relevant is missing.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>
